title: Chameleons Don't Change Color to Hide! 🦎
description: Chameleons don't use pigments to change color — they use tiny crystals under their skin! And discover the real reason they change color.

scenes.say: A chameleon can change color in seconds, from green to yellow to red. How does it do that?

scenes.caption: Crystals under the skin
scenes.say: The secret isn't pigment! Under its skin is a layer of cells packed with tiny crystals arranged in a neat grid.
When it's calm, the crystals sit close together and reflect blue and green. When it gets excited, they spread apart and reflect colors like yellow and red.
People think it changes color to hide. In fact, it mostly does it to signal other chameleons, or to control its body temperature.

scenes.text: Darker colors soak up more sunlight
scenes.say: Did you know when it's cold, it turns darker to absorb more sunlight, just like a black shirt heats up faster in the sun?
